title: Configure and Customize a Nodics Application
readerIntent: Place an application setting at the correct layer and verify it safely.
priorKnowledge: Know the owning capability and the runtime scope that must vary.
owner: Owning capability plus Nodics configuration contracts
summary: Start with the owning module default, override only at the required application or runtime scope, and validate both expected and fallback behavior.

sections.heading: Example decision
paragraphs: Suppose a customer project needs a shorter cache lifetime in local development than in production. The cache capability owns the property name and safe default. The project changes the value in the relevant layered properties.js configuration; it does not copy the cache service or place application behavior in package.json.

sections.heading: Implementation steps
items: Find the capability that owns the behavior and confirm an existing property or extension contract.
Check all existing loaders and override paths before proposing another configuration mechanism.
Keep standard package metadata in package.json and application behavior in properties.js or an explicit runtime-governance contract.
Place secrets in the deployment secret mechanism, never committed source.
Override at the narrowest correct scope and document the default, allowed values, units, restart behavior, and security implications.
Add only the changed property. Do not copy neighboring defaults merely to make the later file appear complete.

sections.heading: Locate the existing authority
items: Search properties.js files and generated configuration context for the capability namespace.
Read the owning module documentation and tests to understand default, type, units, and allowed scopes.
Check project, environment, server, node, tenant, and runtime loaders for an existing override path.
Confirm whether the value is public configuration, a secret reference, or implementation behavior.
Run a duplication check before adding a property with similar meaning.

sections.heading: Worked example
paragraphs: Assume the cache default is appropriate in production but local developers need faster expiry. Add only the local-environment override under the cache-owned namespace. Keep the unit explicit and preserve the production default.

Start startioLocal monoServer, inspect authorized effective configuration or observable cache behavior, and prove the local value. Start another environment or run its configuration test and prove it still receives the default.

The same rule applies to server topology. A server selects active modules, ports, remote endpoints, or an active provider/engine when those differ for that process. It does not repeat an inherited context root, disabled search flag, retry limit, pricing table, or provider endpoint.

sections.heading: Runtime-managed example
paragraphs: For an employee idle-lock timeout stored as an operational setting, define the property contract in the owning BackOffice backend capability. Authorized operations preview and activate the bounded value; Axis consumes the resulting behavior after authentication.
Axis may schedule its lock experience, but it cannot invent or broaden the backend policy. Invalid, unauthorized, expired, conflicting, and rollback behavior remain backend-governed.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Default value when no override exists.
Expected value at the selected environment and topology.
No leakage into another environment, server, node, tenant, or customer.
Invalid type, range, missing dependency, and secret-handling behavior.
Restart and governed runtime-update behavior where supported.
Regression of the original reusable default.

sections.heading: Negative test matrix
items: Unknown property or unsupported layer.
Wrong type, malformed value, zero, negative, or maximum boundary.
Missing referenced provider or dependency.
Secret supplied as literal committed content.
Unauthorized runtime preview, approval, activation, or rollback.
Concurrent update based on a stale version.
Restart with the last valid state after a rejected change.

sections.heading: Documentation and handoff
items: Business meaning and safe default.
Owning capability, namespace, type, unit, range, and example.
Supported override scopes and precedence.
Secret, security, tenant, performance, and cost implications.
Restart, reload, runtime activation, monitoring, and rollback behavior.
Tests and current source evidence.
